## New Cross-Domain Connection

- **[2026-09-28] Today's strategy-feedback finding says the paper-trader's capital-cap rule is quietly cutting value positions at about −7% to −9% after roughly 54 days. The one value-investing case study Fred has actually listened to argues the opposite: a value book has to tolerate a large share of losing positions and long drawdowns.** [[finance/models/model-portfolio-management]] (2026-09-28 Strategy Performance Notes and Pending Strategy Reviews, written today by `strategy-feedback-loop`) found that 11 of 12 paper-trading closes since 09-01 exited at −6.2% to −14.4% and none hit the −15% stop. The cause is daily-paper-trader Step 3F's "exit the weakest position (lowest P&L%)" rule, which fires whenever the book is at the €30k cap. It has hit Strategy A (Value) hardest: PEP, NVO, CMCSA and OTIS were all cut this week as slow bleeders after about 54 days, not because their theses broke. The proposal asks for a per-strategy minimum hold (~90 days for A/F), but it can only cite a gut-feel horizon, and its own caveat admits "we don't know" whether the cuts do harm. [[podcasts/podcast-behind-the-balance-sheet-rich-pzena]] (listened 2026-09-08) supplies the missing practitioner evidence. Two of its four listed themes describe exactly what the rule can't do: "distinguishing temporary business problems from permanent impairment" and "portfolio construction where a meaningful share of positions can lose money and the fund still outperforms." Pzena's firm trailed the S&P by 60pp before recovering. The rule can't make the temporary-vs-permanent distinction because it has no thesis to check: `thesis` coverage is 9/67 for paper-trading-p1, as the same page notes. The 2026-09-12 connection below tied Pzena to Burry's mania playbook. This link is different: it is about the wiki's own mechanical exit rule, and it bears directly on the one open rule-change proposal. Concrete next step: cite the Pzena episode in the 09-28 proposal's *Why* line as the practitioner precedent for option (a), a minimum hold for value strategies. Also note that option (b), "stalest thesis first", can't work until the 9/67 thesis-coverage gap is fixed, because the rule has nothing to rank by.

Saturday full sweep — skimmed the overview/index page of every domain instead of deep-reading one, biasing toward cross-domain connections. A quiet day operationally: email-to-clipping failed (Gmail OAuth token expired/revoked, invalid_grant on search_emails and list_email_labels — needs manual re-auth, not a wiki-thinker fix), and recipe-recommender's weekly batch drew on the same three chefs (Chang, Bourdain, Slater) as every recent run. The only genuinely new source material was today's podcast-summarizer catch-up (4 pages: Prof G Markets on Meta's AI data moat, a David Gardner/Motley Fool interview, and two CyberHack: The Conti Files episodes). Found one real connection: podcasts/podcast-behind-the-balance-sheet-the-fool-david-gardner.md has Gardner stating his core investing heuristics directly — he leans into stocks critics call 'grossly overvalued,' and his best stock-picking rule is buying the top dog/first mover in an emerging industry regardless of price. finance/ideas/idea-ge-vernova.md and finance/ideas/idea-bloom-energy.md each independently describe businesses that fit those exact criteria (GEV explicitly trades '55% above what bullish analysts think it's worth'; Bloom Energy's own scorecard says 'zero margin of safety... traditional value investors should not own this stock') — but both pages read those same facts purely through a single Berkshire-style margin-of-safety lens and land on 'Watch, wait for a pullback,' never engaging the alternative growth-investing framework Gardner represents, where the 'overvalued' consensus is the buy signal, not the reason to wait. Concrete next step: add a line to both idea pages' Verdict sections naming Gardner's framework as the explicit alternative lens being declined, cross-linked from the podcast page. Checked the open sections for resolution: nothing showed clear signs of being actioned since 2026-09-25.
